Timeline::copy_ticks¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

template <std::output_iterator<std::int64_t> OutIt>
void Timeline::copy_ticks(OutIt out) const

Copy Into A Caller-Chosen Destination¶

copy_ticks() writes exact UTC epoch-nanosecond ticks through a C++ output iterator. It is the allocation-policy-neutral export: the caller may append to a vector, fill preallocated memory, or feed another iterator-based component without first accepting the container chosen by an API.

Traversal is logical row-major order and therefore works for contiguous and strided Timelines alike. The method flattens the traversal into the destination; it does not emit shape or timezone metadata. Preserve sizes() and tz() separately when the receiver must later reconstruct both.

Example: Append Exact Ticks¶

#include <pluss/pluss.h>

#include <iostream>
#include <iterator>
#include <vector>

int main() {
  const auto times = pluss::timeline::from_epoch(
      {{-1LL, 0LL}, {1'999'999'999LL, pluss::Timeline::kNaT}});

  std::vector<std::int64_t> ticks;
  times.copy_ticks(std::back_inserter(ticks));

  std::cout << '[';
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < ticks.size(); ++i) {
    if (i) std::cout << ", ";
    std::cout << ticks[i];
  }
  std::cout << "]\n";
}

Output¶

[-1, 0, 1999999999, -9223372036854775808]

No position is suppressed: NaT is copied as Timeline::kNaT, and the matrix is visited left-to-right across each row.

Choosing The Destination¶

With std::back_inserter, reserve numel() elements when allocation behavior matters:

std::vector<std::int64_t> ticks;
ticks.reserve(static_cast<std::size_t>(times.numel()));
times.copy_ticks(std::back_inserter(ticks));

For preallocated storage, the range must have room for exactly numel() writes:

std::vector<std::int64_t> ticks(
    static_cast<std::size_t>(times.numel()));
times.copy_ticks(ticks.begin());

The output-iterator interface cannot inspect the destination capacity. Passing an iterator without sufficient writable space is a caller error.

Guarantees And Boundaries¶

  • Values are copied exactly; no unit conversion or timezone conversion occurs.

  • An empty Timeline performs no writes.

  • A strided source is read in logical order, not raw allocation order.

  • The destination receives neither rank nor shape information.

  • The operation throws if the Timeline is undefined or its tick storage is invalid.

Use ticks() for the convenient owning-vector form. Use epoch_nanos() when shape-preserving numeric computation is the goal.
